eli: Heads-up: Support ticket #12345 — customer Acme reports intermittent 401s immediately after our signing key rotation. They see a spike of failures for ~10-30s then it recovers. Ticket says it correlates with a short 502 from our jwks endpoint.
support-bot: https://support.internal/t/12345 — customer provided logs + a sample JWT.
nora: Can you paste the exact error lines + a sample request? If jwks fetch fails during rotation we might be holding an old cached JWKS and rejecting new kid. Also check client clock skew.
eli: From customer logs (redacted):
```
ERROR auth.verify_signature: signature_verification_failed kid="k_2026-03-13" token_id=... request_id=req-9a1b
WARN jwks.cache: fetch_failed url="https://jwks.redwood.example/.well-known/jwks.json" status=502 retry=0
INFO jwks.cache: using_cached_keys age=4s
INFO auth.verify_signature: signature_verified kid="k_2026-03-13" after_jwks_refresh=false
```
Sample request headers they sent:
```
POST /v1/invoke HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImtfMjAyNi0wMy0xMyJ9....
X-Request-Id: req-9a1b
```
They also attached the JWT header (base64): `\{"alg\":\"RS256\",\"kid\":\"k_2026-03-13\"}`
eli: Repro attempt from their side: they ran ~20 req/s for 40s while we had an upstream 502 for ~3s to the jwks origin. They saw ~8% 401s during that window.
alex: Quick note on current behavior: cache TTL is 300s. On kid-mismatch we do an immediate JWKS fetch but only if last fetch_age > 1s. If the fetch returns 5xx we keep the cached set and fail verification for unseen kids. So if rotation + transient 5xx align you get a short window of rejects. We also don't consider clock skew here (we rely on token iat/exp +- 0s).
nora: That explains it. We should test two fixes: 1) extra small grace period where if we see unknown kid we allow a short ephemeral acceptance for recently rotated kids (with audit logs), and 2) stronger jwks refetch retry/backoff so the fetch is retried a couple times before giving up.
eli: For customer-facing troubleshooting steps I suggested: 1) verify client clock, recommend leeway=10s for clocks, 2) postpone deprecating old kid for 60s after publishing new key, 3) if they can reproduce, collect our /internal/jwks-cache metrics and the jwks origin logs for the window.

nora: Minimal repro script we used locally (inject 502 to jwks origin, then hammer signed endpoint):
```
# in one shell: tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 10ms && ./jwks-orig-proxy --inject-502 3s
# in another shell:
for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SAMPLE_JWT" https://api.local/v1/invoke >/dev/null & done
```
This reliably shows ~some failures when jwks fetch fails briefly.
alex: I'll open a PR for two changes: (A) make jwks fetch retry up to 3 times with short jitter on 5xx/connect-fail (B) on unknown kid, if last successful fetch was <10s ago, try a forced fetch and accept after one successful signature check against newly fetched key, else fail. Also add logging: trace kid mismatch + jwks fetch error details.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch/jwks-refetch-retry (ci: pending) :hourglass: 
eli: Customer update draft: "We're rolling a small runtime change to reduce the chance of brief verification failures during key rotations and to improve retries to the JWKS origin. In the meantime, please confirm client clock, and if you can, keep the old signing key active for an extra minute during rotations." :thumbsup:
aria: +1 (sent to customer).
nora: Follow-up: we should also add metrics for unknown_kid_count and jwks_refetch_failures so support can correlate quickly.
alex: Got it — will include metrics and an alert if unknown_kid_count > 1% of requests in a 1m window.
eli: Thanks all — leaving notes in ticket and attaching repro steps. If customer can reproduce we can run a live debug with them and check origin logs.
